thread.title: Stock Market Action Slows, But Apple Weighs On Market | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stock Market Action Slows, But Apple Weighs On Market | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Volume in the stock market fell Monday, as traders awaited Tuesday's midterm elections. In the meantime, Apple ( AAPL ) gapped down a second straight day, dampening the major indexes' performances.
X The Nasdaq slid 0.9%, while the Dow Jones industrial average and the S&P 500 rose 0.6% and 0.3%, respectively. Small caps in the Russell 2000 lost 0.4%.
Trade sagged about 20% on the NYSE and 30% on the Nasdaq vs. the same time Friday.
Apple's 3% drop late Monday morning had an impact on the major indexes. Apple accounts for 7.5% of the Nasdaq's weighting. The S&P 500 is less sensitive to Apple. Megacap Apple accounts for about 4.1% of the S&P 500. Apple's weighting is almost 15% in the price-based Dow. However, the Dow resisted Apple's drag as 21 of the 30 Dow components rose.
Five stocks in the Dow rose more than 1%. Chevron ( CVX ) added 4%; IBM ( IBM ), 3.5%; McDonald's ( MCD ), 2%; and Travelers ( TRV ) and Procter & Gamble ( PG ), 1.3% and 1.6% respectively.
Two financial companies downgraded Apple on Friday. Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Rosenblatt Securities each downgraded Apple from buy to neutral.
Midterm Elections The midterm elections already could be priced into the market, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 about 10% and 7% off their respective highs. The consensus view is that the Democrats will grab control of the House and the Republicans will keep control of the U.S. Senate.
But surprises are possible. According to the IBD TIPP poll , the Democrats have widened their lead, but President Trump's approval level remained unchanged. The poll was conducted Oct. 25 through Saturday.

Telecom switching systems provider Ciena ( CIEN ) popped 3.8% as it crossed a 32.43 buy point. Volume was 200% above normal. AngloGold Ashanti ( AU ) cleared a 10.39 buy point in volume 150% above average. The stock, though, fell back under the buy point after the initial surge.
Day's Leaders Among IBD's 197 industry groups, the day's leaders included solar, homebuilders and oil companies. On the losing side, automakers, home furnishings and chip groups fell.
